ORAL ORDER

The petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 are before this Court, in the subject petitions, calling in question the charge sheet filed in C.C.No.1858 of 2022, registered for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 324, 326 r/w 34 of the IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 pending on the file of III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The parties to the lis are husband and wife and their relatives.

2. The parties to the lis were also before the Family Court, Bengaluru in M.C.No.5052 of 2022 wherein they have arrived at a settlement and a copy of the memorandum of settlement filed under Order 23 rule 2 r/w Section 151 of the CPC is filed before this Court.

The learned counsel for the NC:
2024:KHC:37363 parties would submit that the conditions stipulated in the settlement are fulfilled.

The relevant paragraphs of memorandum of settlement reads as follows:
".... .... ....
7. The Petitioner hereby unconditionally agrees and undertakes to withdraw all pending cases filed against the respondent and likewise the respondent shall also do so in the better interest of each party.
8.

The Petitioner shall extend her co operation by appearing before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a Petition filed by the Smt Rathna & 4 other in Cri Petition No.3382/2022, seeking quashing of CC.No. 1858/2022 arising out of Crime No 166/2021, for the alleged offences punishable under section 498A, 324, 326 R/w 34 IPC and 3 & 4 of DP Act 1961, pending on the file of the Hon'ble 24th ACMM, Bengaluru.

9. The Petitioner shall also extend her co operation by appearing before the Hon'ble court in a petition to be filed by the respondent seeking quashing seeking quashing of CC.No. 1858/2022, in Crime No 166/2021, pending on the file of the Hon'ble 24th ACMM, Bengaluru, for the alleged offences punishable under section 498A, 324, 326 R/w 34 IPC and 3 & 4 of DP Act 1961, failing which the above mentioned petition shall stands revived and the petitioner shall refund the entire sum of permanent alimony as mentioned above in para 4 with interest.
10. Henceforth either of the parties does have no claims against each other of whatsoever nature either in the movable or immovable NC: 2024:KHC:37363 properties standing in their respective names.

11. This compromise is entered in to between the parties on their free will, consent and volition,
without thereby being any undue influence or otherwise and also based on the advice of their respective learned counsels.

The relevant paragraphs of memorandum of settlement reads as follows:
".... .... ....
7. The Petitioner hereby unconditionally agrees and undertakes to withdraw all pending cases filed against the respondent and likewise the respondent shall also do so in the better interest of each party.
8.
9. The Petitioner shall also extend her co operation by appearing before the Hon'ble court in a petition to be filed by the respondent seeking quashing seeking quashing of CC.No. 1858/2022, in Crime No 166/2021, pending on the file of the Hon'ble 24th ACMM, Bengaluru, for the alleged offences punishable under section 498A, 324, 326 R/w 34 IPC and 3 & 4 of DP Act 1961, failing which the above mentioned petition shall stands revived and the petitioner shall refund the entire sum of permanent alimony as mentioned above in para 4 with interest.
10. Henceforth either of the parties does have no claims against each other of whatsoever nature either in the movable or immovable NC: 2024:KHC:37363 properties standing in their respective names.

without thereby being any undue influence or otherwise and also based on the advice of their respective learned counsels.

Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed.
